edges.description: ZNHIT3 (yeast Hit1) is required for box C/D snoRNP formation, so loss of the protein lowers box C/D snoRNA levels.
znhit3 knockdown and genome editing in zebrafish reproduce edema, but the route from ZNHIT3 loss to edema is not known.
znhit3 loss in zebrafish reproduces microcephaly; in patients head circumference is normal at birth and falls during the first year.
Optic nerve atrophy is a constant neuropathological lesion of PEHO syndrome, but how ZNHIT3 loss damages the optic nerve has not been studied.
Box C/D snoRNPs guide rRNA processing and 2'-O-methylation, so their loss produces processing defects and site-specific hypomethylation.
Defective ribosome production and modification reduces cellular translation.
In Znhit3-knockout cerebellum, rRNA processing defects coincide with nucleolar stress and activation of the p53/p21 pathway.
Blocking p53/p21 signaling rescues granule cell progenitor development, showing that the pathway drives progenitor loss.
Loss of progenitors leaves the granular layer depleted and the cerebellum atrophic.
Granule cell progenitor defects secondarily disturb Purkinje cell alignment and dendritic maturation.
Near-total granule neuron loss is the substrate of the extreme cerebellar atrophy seen on imaging.
Optic nerve degeneration is seen clinically as optic atrophy.
Optic nerve degeneration contributes to blindness; cortical and cerebellar involvement may also contribute and has not been separated.
Loss of znhit3 reproduces the cardinal patient defects.
edges.limitations: Embryonic zebrafish; knockdown and editing do not reproduce the human missense genotype, and later disease course is not assessed.
